# Attachment Endpoint Functions

Reusable compute functions for attachment relationships. `linkParent` establishes an attachment instruction’s return reference to its parent for a `cross-embedded` relationship. It inherits attachment validation, hook compilation and party-access helpers. These functions run when called by an enclosing execution; their availability does not establish anyone’s permission to invoke an operation.

## Linking a parent

`linkParent(input)` takes `input.document`: an exact publication of an existing initialized document, supplied as a Blue ID reference. It reads three fields from the `spec` constant, with no defined defaults:

- `relationship` must be `cross-embedded`; otherwise it rejects with `ATTACHMENT_RETURN_LINK_NOT_NEEDED`.
- `parentOrigin` identifies the parent’s initialized original document at `/contracts/initialized/document`, rather than the supplied publication’s identity.
- `authority` names a required party role. It is not an exclusive caller role.

Document paths refer to the document executing these functions, including an instruction’s own document when nested. Checks on the supplied parent instead read `input.document`.

### Caller and access checks

`requireCaller` first requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to equal `true`, otherwise rejecting with `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. If the executing document has `/activation`, its `active` value must pass the active check, its participant access must remain valid, and `call/channel` must match a party role or a representative channel name of the form `role__repId`. Missing `active` defaults to false for this check. These failures are `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE`, `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING` and `REPRESENTATIVE_NO_LONGER_AUTHORIZED` respectively. If `/activation` is absent, this helper skips those checks; the later roster requirements still apply.

Access checking reads `/activation/accessPaths`, `/activation/readers` and `/activation/parties`, defaulting to an empty list, empty object and empty object respectively. Reader groups combine configured readers with party and representative `readerKeys`; party-derived groups replace configured groups with the same names. Every non-`External Channel` transport must be a `Timeline Channel` supported by one `Timeline Access` record naming its exact timeline, matching its provider, and containing at least one key from every reader group. Separate records cannot collectively satisfy that single-record test. An empty reader group cannot satisfy it. `External Channel` transports bypass this access-record check. Read access does not itself confer operation authority.

### Parent validation and results

The supplied parent must contain `/contracts/initialized/document`; its origin must equal `spec.parentOrigin`, and its `/activation/active` must equal `true`. Failures include `ATTACHMENT_INITIALIZED_DOCUMENT_REQUIRED`, `ATTACHMENT_WRONG_PARENT` and `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_INACTIVE`.

The parent roster must be nonempty. For this cross-embedded link, parent and instruction must have the same party-role set, including `authority`. Corresponding parties must have existing, identical `lead/channel` identities and identical, nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` sets; key order does not matter. Representatives are not compared by this roster check.

After all those checks:

- If `/sources/parent` already exists, its origin must equal `spec.parentOrigin`; a different origin rejects with `ATTACHMENT_REPLACEMENT_FORBIDDEN`. A matching origin returns `outcome: duplicate` without changing the link, even if the newly supplied publication differs. Duplicate attempts still undergo the preceding checks.
- Otherwise, the function appends changes adding `/sources/parent` as a reference to the exact supplied publication and `/attachmentLink` containing `parentOrigin`, then returns `outcome: acceptedNew`.

`acceptedNew` reports that the function prepared those changes. The completed enclosing execution establishes whether they became document state. The function does not emit a linking event.

## Inherited hook configuration

`compileHooks(key, allowed, hooks)` separately compiles hooks grouped by action; every action must appear in `allowed`. Hook names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`, and generated names must not collide.

A hook’s `in` defaults to `instruction`, and `on` defaults to `workflow`. Instruction hooks require workflow mode. Parent hooks require `in: parent` and `on: event` or `on: state`, and compile to embedded bindings at `/sources/parent`. Event hooks require `event`. State hooks require a `path` beginning with `/` and an `equals` value; they use a `Source Changed` match identified by `attachment: key` and an action-and-hook identifier, plus a state-equality guard and the supplied `when`, which defaults to true.

Compiled parent hooks also require the parent to select this instruction’s initialized origin at the configured `instructionPath`. Before execution, they check the parent is active, contains the configured authority, and retains matching primary channels and reader keys. Compilation returns `bindings`, `signals`, `parentDependencies` and `relationship`; the relationship is `cross-embedded` when any hook uses parent scope, otherwise `one-way`. Compilation itself does not establish the return link or emit the signals.

`recheckOn` defaults to an empty list. If explicitly supplied, it is allowed only on parent-state hooks and forbids `before` and `after`. It adds local change bindings for distinct paths beginning with `/`, excluding `/` itself and every path starting with `/sources`. Its `params` and `when` expressions are checked for document-based reevaluation: `$event`, `$binding`, `$var`, `$resultValue`, `$call`, `$const`, `$steps`, `$currentContract`, `$intrinsic`, `$events` and `$changeset` are forbidden, and traversal must finish within 32 rounds.

The separate inherited `businessReady` helper returns true when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires the document not to be closed, every required role approved, recorded terms fields unchanged, and participant access valid. `linkParent` does not invoke this additional readiness test.
